definitions.explanation: The number six. A straightforward number in Japanese with consistent pronunciation in most contexts.

examples.english: I wake up at six o'clock.

examples.japanese: ビールを{六|ろっ}{本|ぽん}ください。
examples.notes: Note: ろく becomes ろっ before ほん→ぽん

examples.japanese: {六|ろく}{月|がつ}は{梅雨|つゆ}の{季節|きせつ}です。
{友達|ともだち}が{六|ろく}{人|にん}{来|き}たので、{椅子|いす}が{足|た}りませんでした。
examples.english: Six friends came, so we didn't have enough chairs.

examples.japanese: {六|ろく}{月|がつ}は{雨|あめ}が{多|おお}いです。{毎日|まいにち}{傘|かさ}を{持|も}って{出|で}かけなければなりません。
examples.english: There's a lot of rain in June. I have to go out with an umbrella every day.

notes:
{六|ろく} is the number six. The native Japanese counting word is {六|むっ}つ (muttsu).

SOUND CHANGES:
When combined with counters starting with h-sounds, ろく often becomes ろっ:
- {六|ろっ}{本|ぽん} (roppon): six long objects
- {六|ろっ}{百|ぴゃく} (roppyaku): 600
- {六|ろっ}{匹|ぴき} (roppiki): six animals

NO CHANGE:
- {六|ろく}{時|じ} (rokuji): six o'clock
- {六|ろく}{人|にん} (rokunin): six people
- {六|ろく}{月|がつ} (rokugatsu): June

CULTURAL NOTE:
Six is generally considered a lucky number in Japan.
